claims.claim: 29% of MATSUlab issues (n=445) were claimed as experiments.

Of 130 claimed experiments in the MATSUlab discourse graph, 50 (38%) produced at least one formal result node, yielding 139 total RES nodes (avg 2.8 per result-producing experiment). 15% of claiming involved cross-person idea exchange, where a different researcher claimed an issue created by someone else.
Among 50 experiments in the MATSUlab that produced formal results, the median time from issue claiming to first result was 12 days, with wide variance (n=50, IQR 0–50 days).
Three undergraduate researchers tracked in this analysis each generated an original result within ~4 months of joining the lab, with two creating a result within ~1 month.

Multiple soluble mediators including IL-5, IL-6, and IFN-γ are significantly elevated in pre-SLE individuals more than 3.5 years before classification, prior to or concurrent with autoantibody positivity.
Innate cytokines, IFN-associated chemokines, and soluble TNF superfamily mediators increase longitudinally in pre-SLE cases approaching classification but not in healthy controls.
BLyS and APRIL levels are comparable in pre-SLE cases and controls until less than 10 months before classification, then increase significantly in cases.
Dysregulation of adaptive immune mediators (IL-4, IL-5, IL-6, IFN-γ, MIG) precedes autoantibody accumulation in preclinical SLE.

Random forest models incorporating ANA and anti-Ro/SSA positivity with IL-5, IL-6, and MIG levels distinguish future SLE patients with 92% accuracy across the entire pre-classification period, compared to 78% accuracy using ANA positivity alone.
A distinct ANA-negative but IL-5/IFN-γ-high pre-SLE cluster is associated with higher risk of nephritis at classification, while ANA-positive cases are more likely to develop arthritis.
Early dysregulation of Th-type cytokines IL-5 (Th2) and IL-6 (Th2/Th17) may be an essential early step in SLE pathogenesis, contributing to all stages of disease.

IFN-γ elevation precedes autoantibodies and drives BLyS/APRIL production, supporting a model where simultaneous dysregulation of T helper, regulatory, IFN-related, and TNF-related pathways erodes immune tolerance.
